header.running_head: Statements of the Sahabah (RA) Concerning the Evil of Dissension

blocks.text: fabricated narrations to cause more disunity). [^1]

Hadhrat Saleem bin Qais Aamiri narrates that Ibnul Kawwaa once asked Hadhrat Ali (RA) about the Sunnah, Bid'ah, unity and disunity. Hadhrat Ali (RA) replied, "O Ibnul Kawwaa! Just as you have memorised the question, so too should you remember the reply. By Allaah, the Sunnaah is the way of Rasulullaah ﷺ while Bid'ah is everything that contradicts it. By Allaah, unity is the consensus of the people of truth even though they may be few while disunity is the consensus of the people of falsehood even though they may be many." [^2]
The Standpoint of the Sahabah (RA) Concerning the Khilaafah after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ
The Sahabah (RA) Unanimously Accept Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) as Khalifah
The Demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sermon of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)

Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) says that (after hearing about the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ) Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) came on his animal from the Sunh district of Madinah. He then dismounted at the door of the Masjid. He was filled with heartache and grief as he sought permission to enter the room of his daughter Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA). When she gave permission, he entered the room where Rasulullaah ﷺ had passed away on the bed. Sitting around Rasulullaah ﷺ were his wives who veiled their faces and concealed themselves from Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Of course, there was no need for Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to do so. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) opened the face of Rasulullaah ﷺ and then knelt on his knees to kiss Rasulullaah ﷺ. He wept as he said, "What the son of Khattaab says is not true[^3]. I swear by the Being Who controls my life that Rasulullaah ﷺ has certainly passed away. May Allaah's mercy be showered on you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ! You are so pure in life and in death!"
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then covered the face of Rasulullaah ﷺ and hastened to the Masjid, skipping over the shoulders of people sitting there until he reached the pulpit. When he saw Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) approach, even Hadhrat Umar (RA) sat down. Standing at the side of the pulpit, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) called the people and they all sat down and kept silent. He recited the Shahaadah as he knew it and said, "Allaah had given the news of the demise of His Nabi ﷺ when he was still alive amongst you. He has also given
Bukhari, Abu Ubayd in Kitaabul Amwaal and Isfahaani in Hujjah, as quoted in Muntakhab (Vol.5 Pg.50).
Askari, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.96).
Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) had been telling people that Rasulullaah ﷺ had not passed away but his soul had merely been transported away to the heavens and would soon return.
